chapters.title: From Horeb to Kadesh
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 1

These Are the Words

1These are the words that Moses spoke to all Israel beyond the Jordan in the wilderness, in the Arabah opposite Suph, between Paran and Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth and Di-zahab.

2It is eleven days' journey from Horeb by the way of Mount Seir to Kadesh-barnea.

3And it came to pass in the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, that Moses spoke to the sons of Israel according to all that the LORD had commanded him for them,

4after he had struck down Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, and Og king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth, at Edrei.

5Beyond the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses undertook to explain this instruction, saying,

Leaving Horeb

6"The LORD our God spoke to us at Horeb, saying, 'You have stayed long enough at this mountain.

7Turn and set out, and go to the hill country of the Amorites and to all their neighbors in the Arabah, in the hill country, in the lowland, in the Negev and on the seacoast, the land of the Canaanites, and Lebanon, as far as the great river, the river Euphrates.

8See, I have set the land before you. Go in and take possession of the land that the LORD swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, to give to them and to their seed after them.'

Judges for the People

9"At that time I said to you, 'I cannot carry you by myself.

10The LORD your God has multiplied you, and today you are as many as the stars of the heavens.

11May the LORD, the God of your fathers, make you a thousand times as many as you are, and bless you as He has promised you!

12How can I bear by myself the weight of you, your burden and your quarrels?

13Choose for yourselves men who are wise, discerning and known among your tribes, and I will make them your heads.'

14You answered me, 'What you have said is good to do.'

15So I took the heads of your tribes, wise men and known, and made them heads over you, commanders of thousands, commanders of hundreds, commanders of fifties and commanders of tens, and officials for your tribes.

16At that time I charged your judges, 'Hear the cases between your brothers, and judge rightly between a man and his brother or the guest who is with him.

17Do not show partiality in judgment. Hear the small and the great alike. Do not be afraid of any man, for the judgment is God's. The case that is too hard for you, bring to me, and I will hear it.'

18At that time I commanded you all the things you should do.

The Scouts at Kadesh

19"We set out from Horeb and went through all that great and terrible wilderness that you saw, by the way of the hill country of the Amorites, as the LORD our God had commanded us, and we came to Kadesh-barnea.

20I said to you, 'You have come to the hill country of the Amorites, which the LORD our God is giving us.

21See, the LORD your God has set the land before you. Go up and take possession, as the LORD, the God of your fathers, has told you. Do not be afraid and do not lose heart.'

22Then all of you came near to me and said, 'Let us send men ahead of us to search out the land for us and bring us back word of the way we should go up and the towns we shall come to.'

23The thing seemed good to me, and I took twelve men from among you, one man for each tribe.

24They turned and went up into the hill country and came to the valley of Eshcol, and scouted it out.

25They took some of the fruit of the land in their hands and brought it down to us, and they brought us back word and said, 'The land that the LORD our God is giving us is good.'

26But you would not go up, and you rebelled against the command of the LORD your God.

27You grumbled in your tents and said, 'Because the LORD hates us He has brought us out of the land of Egypt, to give us into the hand of the Amorites to destroy us.

28Where are we going up to? Our brothers have made our hearts melt, saying, "The people are greater and taller than we are; the cities are great and fortified up to the heavens; and we saw the sons of the Anakim there."'

29I said to you, 'Do not be terrified, and do not be afraid of them.

30The LORD your God, who goes before you, He Himself will fight for you, just as He did for you in Egypt before your eyes,

31and in the wilderness, where you saw how the LORD your God carried you, as a man carries his son, all the way you went until you came to this place.'

32Yet in this you did not trust the LORD your God,

33who went before you on the way to seek out a place for you to camp, in fire by night to show you the way you should go, and in the cloud by day.

The Oath

34"The LORD heard the sound of your words, and He was angry and swore, saying,

35'Not one of these men of this evil generation shall see the good land that I swore to give to your fathers,

36except Caleb son of Jephunneh. He shall see it, and to him and to his sons I will give the land he has walked on, because he has followed the LORD fully.'

37Even with me the LORD was angry on your account, saying, 'You also shall not go in there.

38Joshua son of Nun, who stands before you, he shall go in there. Strengthen him, for he will cause Israel to inherit it.

39Your little ones, who you said would become plunder, and your sons, who today do not know good and evil, they shall go in there. To them I will give it, and they shall possess it.

40But as for you, turn and set out into the wilderness by the way of the Sea of Reeds.'

41Then you answered and said to me, 'We have sinned against the LORD. We will go up and fight, just as the LORD our God commanded us.' Every man of you strapped on his weapons of war and thought it easy to go up into the hill country.

42The LORD said to me, 'Say to them: Do not go up and do not fight, for I am not among you; otherwise you will be struck down before your enemies.'

43So I spoke to you, but you would not listen. You rebelled against the command of the LORD, acted presumptuously and went up into the hill country.

44The Amorites who lived in that hill country came out against you and chased you as bees do, and beat you down in Seir as far as Hormah.

45You came back and wept before the LORD, but the LORD did not listen to your voice or give ear to you.

46So you stayed in Kadesh many days, as many days as you stayed there.

Notes

  • v1 "These are the words" — elleh ha-devarim, the book's opening words and its Hebrew name, Devarim, Words. The Greek name, Deuteronomion, second law, comes from 17:18, where the king is to write mishneh ha-torah ha-zot, a copy of this instruction; mishneh is a second, a double, and the Greek there reads to deuteronomion touto. The book is Moses speaking to Israel: I said to you.

  • v2 "eleven days' journey" — from Horeb to Kadesh by the direct road is eleven days; v3 dates this speech in the fortieth year. The distance between the two numbers is the story of Numbers.

  • v5 "undertook to explain this instruction" — ho'il… be'er, set about to make plain. Be'er is used of writing words very plainly on stones (27:8). Torah here is instruction, the whole teaching Moses is about to give, not yet a name for five books.

  • vv9–18 judges for the people — Moses tells the choosing of the judges in his own words. In Exodus 18 the advice came from his father-in-law Jethro, look among all the people for capable men (Exodus 18:21); here it is Moses who says it to the people, and the burden of Numbers 11:14, I cannot carry all this people by myself, is behind it.

  • v10 "as many as the stars of the heavens" — the promise to Abraham, count the stars… So shall your seed be (Genesis 15:5), spoken as already true: today you are.

  • v17 "the judgment is God's" — ha-mishpat l'Elohim hu. The judge is not to fear a powerful man because the verdict he gives belongs to God.

  • v28 "fortified up to the heavens" — betsurot ba-shamayim, the scouts' words given as the people heard them. In Numbers 13:28 the report was the cities are fortified and very large; by the time it reached the tents, the walls reached the sky.

  • v31 "as a man carries his son" — ka'asher yissa ish et beno, set against v27, where the people say the LORD brought them out because the LORD hates us.

  • v37 "Even with me the LORD was angry on your account" — Numbers 20:12 gives Moses' exclusion as his own failure at the rock, because you did not trust Me. Here Moses says it was on your account, biglalkhem. Both are in the Torah; Deuteronomy gives it from Moses' side.

  • v44 "as bees do" — ka'asher ta'asenah ha-devorim. In Numbers 14:45 the Amalekites and Canaanites struck them and beat them down as far as Hormah; here the attackers are the Amorites and they swarm.

chapters.title: Edom, Moab, Ammon, and Sihon
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 2

Past Esau's Sons

1"Then we turned and set out into the wilderness by the way of the Sea of Reeds, as the LORD had told me, and we went around Mount Seir for many days.

2The LORD said to me,

3'You have gone around this mountain long enough. Turn north.

4Command the people: You are about to pass through the territory of your brothers, the sons of Esau, who live in Seir. They will be afraid of you, so be very careful.

5Do not provoke them, for I will not give you any of their land, not even a footstep, because I have given Mount Seir to Esau as a possession.

6You shall buy food from them with silver, so that you may eat, and you shall also buy water from them with silver, so that you may drink.

7For the LORD your God has blessed you in all the work of your hands. He has known your going through this great wilderness. These forty years the LORD your God has been with you; you have lacked nothing.'

8So we passed by our brothers, the sons of Esau who live in Seir, away from the road of the Arabah, from Elath and Ezion-geber, and we turned and went by the way of the wilderness of Moab.

Moab

9"The LORD said to me, 'Do not harass Moab or provoke them to war, for I will not give you any of their land as a possession, because I have given Ar to the sons of Lot as a possession.'

10(The Emim lived there formerly, a people great and many and tall as the Anakim.

11They too are counted as Rephaim, like the Anakim, but the Moabites call them Emim.

12The Horites also lived in Seir formerly, but the sons of Esau dispossessed them and destroyed them from before them and settled in their place, as Israel did to the land of its possession that the LORD gave them.)

13'Now rise up and cross the Brook Zered.' So we crossed the Brook Zered.

14The time it took us to go from Kadesh-barnea until we crossed the Brook Zered was thirty-eight years, until the whole generation of the men of war had perished from the camp, as the LORD had sworn to them.

15Indeed, the hand of the LORD was against them, to wipe them out from the camp, until they were gone.

Ammon

16"And it came to pass, when all the men of war had died and were gone from among the people,

17that the LORD spoke to me, saying,

18'Today you are to pass through the territory of Moab, through Ar.

19When you come near the sons of Ammon, do not harass them or provoke them, for I will not give you any of the land of the sons of Ammon as a possession, because I have given it to the sons of Lot as a possession.'

20(It too is counted as a land of Rephaim. Rephaim lived there formerly, but the Ammonites call them Zamzummim,

21a people great and many and tall as the Anakim. But the LORD destroyed them from before them, and they dispossessed them and settled in their place,

22as He did for the sons of Esau who live in Seir, when He destroyed the Horites from before them, and they dispossessed them and settled in their place to this day.

23As for the Avvim, who lived in villages as far as Gaza, the Caphtorim, who came out of Caphtor, destroyed them and settled in their place.)

Sihon King of Heshbon

24"'Rise up, set out and cross the Arnon valley. See, I have given into your hand Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land. Begin to take possession, and provoke him to war.

25This day I will begin to put the dread and fear of you on the peoples under the whole heaven, who will hear the report of you and tremble and be in anguish because of you.'

26So I sent messengers from the wilderness of Kedemoth to Sihon king of Heshbon, with words of peace, saying,

27'Let me pass through your land. I will keep to the road; I will not turn aside to the right or to the left.

28You shall sell me food for silver so that I may eat, and give me water for silver so that I may drink. Only let me pass through on foot,

29as the sons of Esau who live in Seir and the Moabites who live in Ar did for me, until I cross the Jordan into the land that the LORD our God is giving us.'

30But Sihon king of Heshbon would not let us pass through his land, for the LORD your God made his spirit hard and his heart stubborn, so that He might give him into your hand, as He has this day.

31The LORD said to me, 'See, I have begun to give Sihon and his land over to you. Begin to take possession, to possess his land.'

32Sihon came out against us, he and all his people, to battle at Jahaz.

33The LORD our God gave him over to us, and we struck him down, with his sons and all his people.

34We captured all his towns at that time and devoted every town to destruction, men, women and little ones. We left no survivor.

35Only the livestock we took as plunder for ourselves, with the spoil of the towns we captured.

36From Aroer, which is on the edge of the Arnon valley, and the town in the valley, as far as Gilead, there was not a town too high for us. The LORD our God gave them all over to us.

37Only the land of the sons of Ammon you did not approach, all the bank of the river Jabbok and the towns of the hill country, and wherever the LORD our God had forbidden us."

Notes

  • v1 "we went around Mount Seir for many days" — va-nasov, we circled. The same verb returns in v3: You have gone around this mountain long enough, rav lakhem sov, the words spoken at Horeb in 1:6, rav lakhem shevet, you have stayed long enough.

  • vv4–6 "your brothers, the sons of Esau" — Edom is brothers because Esau was Jacob's brother. In Numbers 20:14–21 the king of Edom refused passage, Edom came out against them with a large army; this chapter tells of buying food and water from the sons of Esau who live in Seir (vv6, 29) and passing by. The two accounts are given side by side without being joined.

  • v5 "not even a footstep" — ad midrakh kaf ragel, up to the treading of the sole of a foot. Esau's land is as much a gift of the LORD as Israel's: I have given Mount Seir to Esau as a possession.

  • v7 "you have lacked nothing" — lo chasarta davar. Forty years in the wilderness are summed up not as punishment but as provision.

  • vv9, 19 "the sons of Lot" — Moab and Ammon, from Lot's two sons: He is the father of Moab… He is the father of the sons of Ammon to this day (Genesis 19:37–38). Edom, Moab and Ammon are all kin, and all three are left their land.

  • vv10–12, 20–23 the old peoples — the speech breaks off (set in parentheses here) to say who held these lands before: the giants of Moab, Emim, and of Ammon, Zamzummim, both counted among the Rephaim. Genesis 14:5 names the Rephaim and the Emim among the peoples the eastern kings struck; the Horites of Seir are the sons of Seir the Horite (Genesis 36:20). Each people took its land from an older people, and the LORD gave it.

  • v14 "thirty-eight years" — from Kadesh-barnea to the Brook Zered. With the time before Kadesh, it completes the forty years of 1:3, and the oath of 1:35 is kept: that generation is gone.

  • v30 "made his spirit hard and his heart stubborn" — hiqshah… et rucho ve-immets et levavo, the words of Pharaoh's story: I Myself will make Pharaoh's heart hard (Exodus 7:3). Numbers 21:23 says only that Sihon would not let Israel pass; Deuteronomy says why.

  • v34 "devoted every town to destruction" — va-nacharem, from cherem, the vow of Numbers 21:2: I will devote their towns to destruction. What is devoted is given over wholly and nothing is kept, except here the livestock and the spoil (v35).

chapters.title: Og of Bashan, and Moses' Plea
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 3

Og King of Bashan

1"Then we turned and went up by the road to Bashan, and Og king of Bashan came out against us, he and all his people, to battle at Edrei.

2The LORD said to me, 'Do not be afraid of him, for I have given him into your hand, with all his people and his land. You shall do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon.'

3So the LORD our God gave into our hand Og king of Bashan as well, with all his people, and we struck him down until no survivor was left to him.

4We captured all his towns at that time. There was not a town that we did not take from them: sixty towns, the whole region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.

5All these were towns fortified with high walls, gates and bars, besides a great many unwalled villages.

6We devoted them to destruction, as we had done to Sihon king of Heshbon, devoting every town to destruction, men, women and little ones.

7But all the livestock and the spoil of the towns we took as plunder for ourselves.

8So at that time we took the land out of the hand of the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, from the Arnon valley to Mount Hermon

9(the Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir),

10all the towns of the plateau, all Gilead and all Bashan, as far as Salecah and Edrei, towns of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.

11(For only Og king of Bashan was left of the remnant of the Rephaim. His bed was a bed of iron; is it not in Rabbah of the sons of Ammon? Nine cubits was its length and four cubits its width, by the cubit of a man.)

The Land Divided East of the Jordan

12"This land we took possession of at that time. From Aroer, which is by the Arnon valley, and half the hill country of Gilead with its towns, I gave to the Reubenites and the Gadites.

13The rest of Gilead, and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og, I gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh — the whole region of Argob, all Bashan; it is called a land of Rephaim.

14Jair son of Manasseh took the whole region of Argob as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and called them after his own name, Havvoth-jair — Bashan — to this day.

15To Machir I gave Gilead.

16To the Reubenites and the Gadites I gave from Gilead as far as the Arnon valley, with the middle of the valley as a border, and as far as the river Jabbok, the border of the sons of Ammon,

17and the Arabah, with the Jordan as a border, from Chinnereth as far as the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, under the slopes of Pisgah on the east.

18At that time I commanded you, saying, 'The LORD your God has given you this land to possess. All you men of valor shall cross over armed before your brothers, the sons of Israel.

19Only your wives, your little ones and your livestock — I know that you have much livestock — shall stay in the towns I have given you,

20until the LORD gives rest to your brothers as He has to you, and they too possess the land that the LORD your God is giving them beyond the Jordan. Then each of you may return to his possession that I have given you.'

21At that time I commanded Joshua, saying, 'Your eyes have seen all that the LORD your God has done to these two kings. So the LORD will do to all the kingdoms into which you are crossing.

22Do not be afraid of them, for the LORD your God is the one who fights for you.'

Moses' Plea

23"At that time I pleaded with the LORD, saying,

24'Lord GOD, You have begun to show Your servant Your greatness and Your strong hand. For what god is there in heaven or on earth who can do works and mighty deeds like Yours?

25Let me cross over, please, and see the good land beyond the Jordan, that good hill country and Lebanon.'

26But the LORD was furious with me on your account and would not listen to me. The LORD said to me, 'Enough! Speak to Me no more of this matter.

27Go up to the top of Pisgah and lift your eyes to the west and to the north and to the south and to the east, and look with your eyes, for you shall not cross this Jordan.

28But command Joshua, and strengthen him and encourage him, for he shall cross over before this people, and he shall cause them to inherit the land that you will see.'

29So we stayed in the valley opposite Beth-peor."

Notes

  • vv1–3 Og — the battle of Numbers 21:33–35 told again in almost the same words: Do not be afraid of him, for I have given him into your hand… You shall do to him as you did to Sihon. Here it is Moses remembering, the LORD said to me.

  • v9 "the Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir" — one mountain with three names, like the peoples of 2:10–12 and 2:20, each with its own name for the same giants.

  • v11 "His bed was a bed of iron" — eres barzel. Og is the remnant of the Rephaim, the old giant peoples of 2:11, and his bed is given as proof: nine cubits by four, by the cubit of a man, the ordinary forearm. Is it not in Rabbah? speaks to readers who could go and see it.

  • v14 "Havvoth-jair" — the name Numbers 32:41 gives to Jair's tent villages; here it is laid over all of Argob, Bashan, to this day.

  • v17 "the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea" — two names for one lake, the second the name of Genesis 14:3 and Numbers 34:3.

  • v20 "until the LORD gives rest to your brothers" — yaniach, gives rest, from nuach. The eastern tribes may go home only when the others have rest too.

  • v24 "Lord GOD" — Adonai YHWH, the address Abram uses in Genesis 15:2, Lord GOD, what will You give me? Both men open a request to God with it.

  • vv25–27 "Let me cross over… the LORD was furious… you shall not cross" — e'berah, let me cross, from avar; va-yit'abber, was furious, a verb built on the same three letters; and lo ta'avor, you shall not cross. The plea and the refusal are made of one word.

  • v26 "Enough!" — rav lakh, much for you, the words of 1:6 and 2:3, You have stayed long enough, You have gone around… long enough, now said to Moses about his own prayer.

  • v27 "lift your eyes to the west and to the north and to the south and to the east" — what the LORD told Abram after Lot left him: Lift up, please, your eyes, and look from the place where you are — northward and southward and eastward and seaward (Genesis 13:14). Abram was told the land he saw would be his; Moses may only see it.

chapters.title: You Saw No Form
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 4

Hear the Statutes

1"And now, Israel, listen to the statutes and the rules that I am teaching you to do, so that you may live, and go in and take possession of the land that the LORD, the God of your fathers, is giving you.

2You shall not add to the word that I command you, and you shall not take away from it, so that you keep the commandments of the LORD your God that I command you.

3Your eyes have seen what the LORD did at Baal-peor, for the LORD your God destroyed from among you every man who followed the Baal of Peor.

4But you who held fast to the LORD your God are all alive today.

5See, I have taught you statutes and rules, as the LORD my God commanded me, for you to do in the land you are going in to possess.

6Keep them and do them, for that will be your wisdom and your understanding in the eyes of the peoples, who will hear all these statutes and say, 'Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.'

7For what great nation is there that has a god so near to it as the LORD our God is whenever we call on Him?

8What great nation is there that has statutes and rules as righteous as all this instruction that I set before you today?

The Day at Horeb

9"Only take care, and guard yourself closely, so that you do not forget the things your eyes have seen, and so that they do not depart from your heart all the days of your life. Make them known to your sons and your sons' sons —

10the day you stood before the LORD your God at Horeb, when the LORD said to me, 'Gather the people to Me, and I will let them hear My words, so that they may learn to fear Me all the days they live on the earth, and may teach their sons.'

11You came near and stood at the foot of the mountain, and the mountain burned with fire to the heart of the heavens, with darkness, cloud and thick darkness.

12The LORD spoke to you from the middle of the fire. You heard the sound of words, but you saw no form; there was only a voice.

13He declared to you His covenant, which He commanded you to do, the Ten Words, and He wrote them on two tablets of stone.

14The LORD commanded me at that time to teach you statutes and rules, for you to do them in the land you are crossing over to possess.

No Image

15"So take great care for your lives, since you saw no form on the day the LORD spoke to you at Horeb from the middle of the fire,

16so that you do not act corruptly and make for yourselves a carved image in the form of any figure, the likeness of male or female,

17the likeness of any animal that is on the earth, the likeness of any winged bird that flies in the sky,

18the likeness of anything that creeps on the ground, the likeness of any fish that is in the waters under the earth;

19and so that you do not lift your eyes to the heavens and see the sun, the moon and the stars, all the host of heaven, and be drawn away and bow down to them and serve them, things the LORD your God has allotted to all the peoples under the whole heaven.

20But the LORD has taken you and brought you out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, to be a people of His own inheritance, as you are this day.

21The LORD was angry with me because of you, and He swore that I would not cross the Jordan and would not go into the good land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.

22For I am to die in this land. I am not crossing the Jordan; but you are crossing, and you shall possess this good land.

23Take care for yourselves, so that you do not forget the covenant of the LORD your God, which He made with you, and make for yourselves a carved image in the form of anything the LORD your God has forbidden you.

24For the LORD your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God.

Scattered and Sought

25"When you have fathered sons and sons' sons, and have grown old in the land, and you act corruptly and make a carved image in the form of anything, and do what is evil in the eyes of the LORD your God, provoking Him to anger,

26I call heaven and earth to witness against you today that you will quickly perish from the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess. You will not live long on it; you will be utterly destroyed.

27The LORD will scatter you among the peoples, and you will be left few in number among the nations where the LORD will drive you.

28There you will serve gods made by human hands, wood and stone, which neither see nor hear nor eat nor smell.

29But from there you will seek the LORD your God, and you will find Him, if you search for Him with all your heart and with all your soul.

30When you are in distress and all these things have come upon you, in the end of days you will return to the LORD your God and listen to His voice.

31For the LORD your God is a merciful God. He will not let you go, and He will not destroy you, and He will not forget the covenant with your fathers that He swore to them.

There Is No Other

32"For ask now about the former days, which were before you, from the day that God created humankind on the earth, and from one end of the heavens to the other: has anything as great as this ever happened, or has anything like it ever been heard of?

33Has any people ever heard the voice of God speaking from the middle of the fire, as you have heard, and lived?

34Or has any god ever tried to go and take for himself a nation from the middle of another nation, by trials, by signs and by wonders, by war, by a strong hand and an outstretched arm, and by great terrors, as all that the LORD your God did for you in Egypt before your eyes?

35You were shown it so that you might know that the LORD is God; there is no other besides Him.

36From heaven He let you hear His voice, to discipline you, and on earth He let you see His great fire, and you heard His words from the middle of the fire.

37Because He loved your fathers, He chose their seed after them, and He Himself brought you out of Egypt by His great strength,

38to drive out before you nations greater and mightier than you, to bring you in and give you their land as an inheritance, as it is this day.

39Know therefore today, and lay it to your heart, that the LORD is God in heaven above and on the earth below; there is no other.

40Keep His statutes and His commandments, which I command you today, so that it may go well with you and with your sons after you, and so that you may live long on the ground that the LORD your God is giving you for all time."

Three Towns of Refuge

41Then Moses set apart three towns beyond the Jordan, toward the sunrise,

42for the one who kills his neighbor unintentionally, without having hated him before, to flee there, so that he may flee to one of these towns and live:

43Bezer in the wilderness on the plateau, for the Reubenites; Ramoth in Gilead, for the Gadites; and Golan in Bashan, for the Manassites.

The Instruction

44This is the instruction that Moses set before the sons of Israel.

45These are the testimonies, the statutes and the rules that Moses spoke to the sons of Israel when they came out of Egypt,

46beyond the Jordan, in the valley opposite Beth-peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, whom Moses and the sons of Israel struck down when they came out of Egypt.

47They took possession of his land and the land of Og king of Bashan, the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise,

48from Aroer, which is on the edge of the Arnon valley, as far as Mount Sion, that is, Hermon,

49with all the Arabah beyond the Jordan on the east, as far as the Sea of the Arabah, under the slopes of Pisgah.

Notes

  • v2 "You shall not add… and you shall not take away" — lo tosifu… ve-lo tigre'u. Gara, to take away, is the verb of the daughters of Zelophehad and the heads of their clan (Numbers 27:4; 36:3). The instruction is to be handed on whole.

  • v4 "you who held fast to the LORD" — ha-deveqim, from davaq, to cling, the verb of Genesis 2:24, clings to his woman. At Peor Israel yoked itself to Baal (Numbers 25:3); those who clung to the LORD instead are the ones still alive.

  • v12 "you saw no form; there was only a voice" — u-temunah einkhem ro'im zulati qol. The whole argument of vv15–24 rests on this sentence: at Horeb nothing was seen, so nothing may be made. Temunah, form, likeness, is the word of the commandment, any form of what is in the heavens (Exodus 20:4).

  • v13 "the Ten Words" — aseret ha-devarim, the ten words, the Bible's own name for what English calls the Ten Commandments.

  • vv16–18 male or female… animal… bird… creeping thing… fish — the creatures of Genesis 1 in reverse order: God made the fish and birds, then the animals and creeping things, then humankind male and female (Genesis 1:20–27). Here the list starts with male or female and ends with fish. Nothing that God made may be made into an image of Him.

  • v19 "things the LORD your God has allotted to all the peoples" — asher chalaq, which He divided, apportioned to every people under heaven. Israel is not to bow to them; what the other peoples were given them for, the verse does not say. Verse 20 sets Israel apart: But the LORD has taken you.

  • v20 "the iron furnace" — kur ha-barzel, the smelting furnace in which iron is refined. Egypt was the fire Israel was brought out of.

  • v24 "a consuming fire, a jealous God" — esh okhlah hu, El qanna: the consuming fire of Exodus 24:17, the look of the LORD's glory was like a consuming fire on the top of the mountain, and the jealous God of the commandment (Exodus 20:5).

  • v30 "in the end of days" — be-acharit ha-yamim, the phrase of Jacob's blessing, what will befall you in the end of days (Genesis 49:1), and of Balaam's last oracle (Numbers 24:14). Here it looks past exile to a return.

  • v42 "without having hated him before" — mi-temol shilshom, from yesterday and the day before: there was no old grudge. The towns of refuge of Numbers 35 are set apart for the eastern tribes; the three in Canaan come later.

chapters.title: The Ten Words
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 5

The Covenant at Horeb

1Moses called all Israel and said to them, "Hear, Israel, the statutes and the rules that I speak in your hearing today. Learn them and be careful to do them.

2The LORD our God made a covenant with us at Horeb.

3Not with our fathers did the LORD make this covenant, but with us, we who are all here alive today.

4Face to face the LORD spoke with you on the mountain from the middle of the fire,

5while I stood between the LORD and you at that time to declare to you the word of the LORD, for you were afraid because of the fire and did not go up the mountain. He said:

The Ten Words

6'I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slaves.

7You shall have no other gods before My face.

8You shall not make for yourself a carved image, any form of what is in the heavens above, or on the earth below, or in the waters under the earth.

9You shall not bow down to them and you shall not serve them — because I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, calling the guilt of fathers to account on sons, on the third and on the fourth generation of those who hate Me,

10and doing loyal love to thousands, for those who love Me and keep My commandments.

11You shall not lift up the name of the LORD your God for emptiness, because the LORD will not leave unpunished the one who lifts up His name for emptiness.

12Keep the sabbath day, to keep it holy, as the LORD your God commanded you.

13Six days you shall work and do all your labor,

14but the seventh day is a sabbath to the LORD your God. You shall not do any labor — you, or your son, or your daughter, or your male slave, or your female slave, or your ox, or your donkey, or any of your animals, or the guest who is inside your gates — so that your male slave and your female slave may rest as you do.

15Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God brought you out from there with a strong hand and an outstretched arm. That is why the LORD your God commanded you to keep the sabbath day.

16Honor your father and your mother, as the LORD your God commanded you, so that your days may be long, and so that it may go well with you on the ground that the LORD your God is giving you.

17You shall not murder.

18You shall not commit adultery.

19You shall not steal.

20You shall not answer against your neighbor as an empty witness.

21You shall not covet your neighbor's wife. You shall not desire your neighbor's house, his field, or his male slave, or his female slave, his ox, or his donkey, or anything that is your neighbor's.'

Speak to Us Yourself

22"These words the LORD spoke to all your assembly on the mountain from the middle of the fire, the cloud and the thick darkness, with a loud voice, and He added no more. He wrote them on two tablets of stone and gave them to me.

23And it came to pass, when you heard the voice from the middle of the darkness, while the mountain was burning with fire, that you came near to me, all the heads of your tribes and your elders,

24and said, 'The LORD our God has shown us His glory and His greatness, and we have heard His voice from the middle of the fire. Today we have seen that God may speak with a human being and he may live.

25And now, why should we die? For this great fire will consume us. If we hear the voice of the LORD our God any more, we will die.

26For who of all flesh has heard the voice of the living God speaking from the middle of the fire, as we have, and lived?

27You go near and hear all that the LORD our God says, and you speak to us all that the LORD our God speaks to you, and we will hear and do it.'

28The LORD heard the sound of your words when you spoke to me, and the LORD said to me, 'I have heard the sound of the words of this people, which they have spoken to you. All that they have said is good.

29If only they had such a heart as this always, to fear Me and keep all My commandments, so that it might go well with them and with their sons forever!

30Go, say to them, "Return to your tents."

31But you, stand here by Me, and I will speak to you all the commandment, the statutes and the rules that you shall teach them, so that they may do them in the land I am giving them to possess.'

32So be careful to do as the LORD your God has commanded you. Do not turn aside to the right or to the left.

33Walk in all the way that the LORD your God has commanded you, so that you may live, and it may go well with you, and you may live long in the land you shall possess."

Notes

  • v3 "Not with our fathers… but with us, we who are all here alive today" — most of those who stood at Horeb have died in the wilderness (2:14–16). Moses speaks to their children as if they had been there: the covenant is made with whoever hears it today.

  • v4 "Face to face" — panim be-fanim, and yet v5 says Moses stood between, and 4:12 that they saw no form. The phrase is about the directness of the speaking, not about seeing.

  • v12 "Keep the sabbath day" — shamor, where Exodus 20:8 has zakhor, Remember. Deuteronomy adds as the LORD your God commanded you, pointing back to Sinai; the command is being repeated, not given for the first time.

  • vv14–15 the reason for the sabbath — in Exodus 20:11 the reason is creation: in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth… and He rested on the seventh day. Here it is Egypt: Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, so that your male slave and your female slave may rest as you do. The same day is grounded once in God's rest and once in Israel's release.

  • v16 "and so that it may go well with you" — words Exodus 20:12 does not have. Deuteronomy's own refrain returns in v29 and v33.

  • vv18–21 "You shall not… You shall not" — in the Hebrew, each of these commands begins with and: ve-lo tin'af, ve-lo tignov, and you shall not… and you shall not, joining them into one chain. Exodus has no and.

  • v20 "as an empty witness" — ed shav, where Exodus 20:16 has ed shaqer, a false witness. Shav is the word of v11, for emptiness: testimony with nothing behind it.

  • v21 the wife first, and two verbs — Exodus 20:17 puts the house first and the wife among the household. Here the wife stands alone with her own verb, lo tachmod, you shall not covet, and the house, now with his field, gets another: lo tit'avveh, you shall not desire.

  • v22 "and He added no more" — ve-lo yasaf: the ten were spoken aloud to all the people, and then the voice stopped. Everything after comes through Moses (v31).

  • v29 "If only they had such a heart as this always" — mi yitten, who will give, the Hebrew form of a wish. God wishes the people's fear at the mountain would last.

speech.text: Deuteronomy 5
The Covenant at Horeb
Moses called all Israel and said to them, "Hear, Israel, the statutes and the rules that I speak in your hearing today. Learn them and be careful to do them.
The LORD our God made a covenant with us at Horeb.
Not with our fathers did the LORD make this covenant, but with us, we who are all here alive today.
Face to face the LORD spoke with you on the mountain from the middle of the fire,
while I stood between the LORD and you at that time to declare to you the word of the LORD, for you were afraid because of the fire and did not go up the mountain. He said:
The Ten Words
'I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slaves.
You shall have no other gods before My face.
You shall not make for yourself a carved image, any form of what is in the heavens above, or on the earth below, or in the waters under the earth.

You shall not bow down to them and you shall not serve them — because I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, calling the guilt of fathers to account on sons, on the third and on the fourth generation of those who hate Me,
and doing loyal love to thousands, for those who love Me and keep My commandments.
You shall not lift up the name of the LORD your God for emptiness, because the LORD will not leave unpunished the one who lifts up His name for emptiness.
Keep the sabbath day, to keep it holy, as the LORD your God commanded you.
Six days you shall work and do all your labor,

but the seventh day is a sabbath to the LORD your God. You shall not do any labor — you, or your son, or your daughter, or your male slave, or your female slave, or your ox, or your donkey, or any of your animals, or the guest who is inside your gates — so that your male slave and your female slave may rest as you do.

Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God brought you out from there with a strong hand and an outstretched arm. That is why the LORD your God commanded you to keep the sabbath day.
Honor your father and your mother, as the LORD your God commanded you, so that your days may be long, and so that it may go well with you on the ground that the LORD your God is giving you.
You shall not murder.
You shall not commit adultery.
You shall not steal.
You shall not answer against your neighbor as an empty witness.
You shall not covet your neighbor's wife. You shall not desire your neighbor's house, his field, or his male slave, or his female slave, his ox, or his donkey, or anything that is your neighbor's.'
Speak to Us Yourself

"These words the LORD spoke to all your assembly on the mountain from the middle of the fire, the cloud and the thick darkness, with a loud voice, and He added no more. He wrote them on two tablets of stone and gave them to me.
And it came to pass, when you heard the voice from the middle of the darkness, while the mountain was burning with fire, that you came near to me, all the heads of your tribes and your elders,

and said, 'The LORD our God has shown us His glory and His greatness, and we have heard His voice from the middle of the fire. Today we have seen that God may speak with a human being and he may live.
And now, why should we die? For this great fire will consume us. If we hear the voice of the LORD our God any more, we will die.
For who of all flesh has heard the voice of the living God speaking from the middle of the fire, as we have, and lived?
You go near and hear all that the LORD our God says, and you speak to us all that the LORD our God speaks to you, and we will hear and do it.'

The LORD heard the sound of your words when you spoke to me, and the LORD said to me, 'I have heard the sound of the words of this people, which they have spoken to you. All that they have said is good.
If only they had such a heart as this always, to fear Me and keep all My commandments, so that it might go well with them and with their sons forever!
Go, say to them, "Return to your tents."
But you, stand here by Me, and I will speak to you all the commandment, the statutes and the rules that you shall teach them, so that they may do them in the land I am giving them to possess.'
So be careful to do as the LORD your God has commanded you. Do not turn aside to the right or to the left.
Walk in all the way that the LORD your God has commanded you, so that you may live, and it may go well with you, and you may live long in the land you shall possess."
